title: Proving Existence of a Root using IVT
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use the Intermediate Value Theorem to prove that the polynomial equation x^3 - 3x - 1 = 0 has a real solution in the interval [1, 2].

steps.title: Verify Continuity Hypothesis
steps.explanation: Every polynomial is continuous everywhere on the real line, including the closed interval [1, 2].
steps.why: Hypothesis of IVT requires continuity on [a, b].

steps.title: Evaluate at the Interval Endpoints
steps.explanation: Compute the function values at the endpoints.
steps.why: Endpoint values establish the sign change across the interval.

steps.title: Apply the Intermediate Value Theorem
steps.mathExpression: f(1) = -3 < 0 < 1 = f(2) \implies \exists c \in (1, 2) \text{ such that } f(c) = 0
steps.explanation: Because 0 is between f(1) and f(2), there must exist a c in (1, 2) with f(c) = 0.
steps.why: Direct conclusion of the Intermediate Value Theorem.
